messages.author: 9403604069d4685f
messages.subject: Testlet modeling in lavaan
parts:
Hi,

I am looking to apply the testlet model by Bradlow, Wainer & Wang (1999) in lavaan.

Under this model, the response of person i to item j Y_ij = logit^-1(t_ij)

ignore the logit part, I will deal with this later, but the problem lies with the fact that t_ij is defined as:

a_j*(theta_i  - b_j - gamma_id(j)),

where a is the item discrimination, b is the difficulty, theta is the latent trait, gamma is the testlet effect and d is the indicator denoting to which of the testlets does the item belong (e.g. 1st testlet, 2nd testlet...).

As you can see, gamma is defined not just as an item parameter, but also a person parameter. Thus, writing a model like this:

F =~ Y1 + Y2 + Y3 + Y4 + Y5 + Y6

Y1 | (b + tl1*gamma)
Y2 | (b + tl1*gamma)
Y3 | (b + tl1*gamma)

Y4 | (b + tl2*gamma)
Y5 | (b + tl2*gamma)
Y6 | (b + tl2*gamma)

Wouldn't work because then the testlet is going to be just an item parameter. What is the proper way to define this testlet model in lavaan?

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Testlet modeling in lavaan
parts:
I am afraid you can't do this with lavaan. It looks like you need
'definition variables'. I would suggest to try the OpenMx package. It
was designed to handle cases like this.

Yves.
